text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (likely evolving from generalized absence seizures).

The detailed history of staring spells lasting 3-4 minutes, post-ictal confusion, and a specific "muddy taste" strongly suggests complex partial or generalized seizures with secondary generalization. Given the duration and post-ictal state, this is concerning for status epilepticus. I am requesting an EEG and MRI Brain immediately to confirm the diagnosis and rule out structural causes.
